items.t: ‘One step at a time’: ‘The Kapil Sharma Show’ actress Sumona Chakravarti returns to gym six months after e
sum: has offered fans a glimpse into her fitness comeback, returning to the gym six months after undergoing surgery for endometriosis. The actor recently posted a workout video on Instagram, sharing that her doctor and physiotherapist had finally given her the go-ahead to resume exercising.

Sumona had spoken about her battle with endometriosis and revealed in a detailed social media post in July that she had undergone surgery for the condition. Her health challenges had also prompted her to take a break from social media for some time. Now, as she gradually gets back to her fitness routine, the actor has shared an update on her recovery with her followers.

On her first day back at the gym, Sumona also managed to run for the first time in a long while. The actor shared a video of her workout routine on social media, giving followers a glimpse of how she is gradually rebuilding her fitness after surgery.

Describing her first running session, she wrote on the video, "After a full leg workout, i ran today finally. After a very long time. 4 mins run + 1 min walk - x4 20 mins & i was dead. But it was Day 1...This is what re start looks like. Slowly & Steadily. (sic)."
Alongside the video, Sumona also shared an update on her recovery, revealing that she had completed six months since her operation and received medical clearance to return to physical activity.

Sharing her thoughts on getting back into shape, the actress captioned the post, "6 months post op. Full clearance from my doctor & physical therapist. Time to start shredding. Body is definitely looking & feeling very different. I’m trying to understand it all over again. One step at a time. (sic)."

Philips Advances AI Imaging Workflows With New Cloud-Based Solution
sum: Koninklijke Philips PHG recently introduced Philips Advanced Image Insights on HealthSuite, a cloud-based solution that combines advanced visualization applications with centralized management and orchestration of third-party AI applications for medical imaging. Connected to Philips HealthSuite Imaging, the platform is designed to automate workflows, integrate analysis results into existing radiology systems and streamline structured reporting. The launch aims to help radiology teams manage growing imaging volumes and increasingly complex diagnostic workflows more efficiently.

Per management, the opportunity in radiology lies not simply in adding more AI applications but in connecting intelligence across the diagnostic process. Integrating advanced visualization and AI tools could reduce manual work, provide clinicians with better access to relevant insights and allow them to devote more time to reviewing images and making informed care decisions.
Year to date, the stock has gained 10.2% against the industry’s 14.9% fall. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 has risen 3.9% during the same timeframe.

The launch could strengthen Philips' competitive position in the expanding market for AI-enabled medical imaging solutions. By bringing multiple imaging applications together through a unified cloud platform, the company could make its digital offerings more valuable to healthcare organizations seeking to modernize radiology operations. The solution may also help Philips expand its software-as-a-service opportunities, increase engagement with existing imaging customers and attract providers looking for scalable enterprise imaging solutions.
PHG currently has a market capitalization of $29.33 billion.

Advanced Image Insights provides access to Philips and third-party AI-powered image analysis applications across supported imaging modalities and clinical specialties. Integrated with Philips HealthSuite Imaging PACS, the platform automates the transfer of studies to relevant applications and makes their analysis results available within existing radiology workflows. This allows radiologists to review AI-generated findings alongside diagnostic images.

items.t: Gree Veteran Ramps Up Investment in Philips Air Conditioners
sum: Business is akin to a battlefield, and the most dramatic scenario is none other than former long-time partners becoming new rivals today.

Tianyancha shows that Anhui Enbili Electric Appliance Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Enbili"), the Chinese operator of Philips air conditioners, has recently completed a series of industrial and commercial changes, with the legal representative of the company changed from Xu Ligen to Xu Zifa.

According to Tianyancha, Hebei Gree Electric Appliance Marketing Co., Ltd. is jointly held by Hebei Guoao Investment Group Co., Ltd. and Hebei Xinxing Gree Electric Appliance Sales Co., Ltd. Xu Zifa holds 25% of the shares of "Hebei Xinxing Gree", and indirectly holds 20% of the shares of "Hebei Gree Electric Appliance Marketing" through Shijiazhuang Huafang Deyi Renewable Resources Development Co., Ltd.
After this round of capital increase and share expansion, Xu Zifa has obtained actual control of Enbili and become the leader of Philips air conditioner business in China.

What is more thought-provoking is that Xu Zifa was originally the general distributor of Hebei region and also a long-time partner under Dong Mingzhu. However, the two parted ways in 2022, and before that, Xu Zifa had intervened in the Chinese business of Philips air conditioners as an investor.

Now four years later, the entire air conditioning industry is having a hard time, but Xu Zifa has chosen to increase his investment against the trend. What on earth is this veteran who has served Gree for most of his life betting on?
In the distribution system circle of Gree, Xu Zifa is an unavoidable name.

items.t: Commentary: Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia makes everyone involved look corrupt
sum: You’re going to see not a few news stories and cable discussions trying to identify the winners and losers from Jensen Huang’s shock reinstatement Monday as chief executive of the AI chipmaker Nvidia after his 11 days in the wilderness.
Allow me to make it easier for you: There are no winners. Almost everyone involved in this episode comes out of it bathed in a miasma of corruption and ineptitude.
Chief among them are the members of Nvidia’s board and the cabal of tech bros such as Elon Musk, who publicly agitated for Huang’s return.
When a board of directors can no longer trust a chief executive, removal is their duty.

Then there are the White House insiders who supported Huang, such as Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, and those who celebrated his ouster but then dutifully celebrated his return, like Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

And President Trump, who is taking credit for goading the Nvidia directors into welcoming back a CEO who slathered them with flagrant lies about personal activities that may have involved complicity with a chip-smuggling scheme that may have violated U.S. law. Anyway, Trump gained as much as $15 million when his Nvidia holdings soared higher Monday.

“It’s lose-lose-lose,” Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, senior associate dean for Leadership Studies at the Yale School of Management, says of the Huang mess. “It’s indisputably a degradation of national security,” given the suspicions that Huang was involved in the transfer of U.S. technology to China. It will turbocharge congressional investigations of those allegations — with considerable pressure for the investigations coming from Republicans.

Philips stock: Seeking Alpha keeps Buy view on strong orders
sum: Seeking Alpha published a new analysis of Koninklijke Philips N.V. on Monday, November 23, 2026, maintaining a Buy view on the company as stronger orders and expanding margins support the recovery case. The study was written by Mare Evidence Lab and links the positive stance to Philips' operating progress and valuation.

The analysis highlights third-quarter comparable equipment order intake growth of 8% and nearly 20% growth in Diagnosis & Treatment orders. It also points to adjusted EBITA of EUR 569 million and quarterly productivity savings of EUR 170 million. Savings for the first nine months reached EUR 427 million, strengthening the case for further margin improvement.

Seeking Alpha also notes that Philips' third-quarter sales increased 2%. The Respironics settlement provision weighed on reported profitability, leaving the recalled sleep and respiratory devices business as a continuing source of legal and financial risk.

The current investment case therefore rests on operating execution rather than a change in the company's formal outlook. Stronger hospital-equipment demand, productivity measures and improving profitability support the bullish view, while litigation exposure and the financial consequences of the Respironics recall remain important counterweights.

The latest analysis follows earlier Philips coverage after the second-quarter results and says the shares have gained 10% since that update. That performance has not removed the valuation debate, but the author continues to see upside and retains the Buy rating. Investors will continue to weigh order growth against execution risks, settlement costs and the pace of improvement in the affected businesses.

Ottawa Charge embrace roster changes in pursuit of elusive Walter Cup title
sum: OTTAWA — The Ottawa Charge are entering the 2026-27 PWHL season with a new home, a revamped roster and hopes of making a third straight appearance in the Walter Cup final.

The Charge have lost several key players, including captain Brianne Jenner and forward Emily Clark, who both signed with the expansion Hamilton Havoc. But general manager Mike Hirshfeld sees an opportunity for others to step into bigger roles.

“It’s disappointing, but we’re super excited about the group we brought in and feel like we have a lot of great players, young players that are ready to take that next step,” said Hirshfeld. “So, we’re back at it, and we’re reloading and going for the Walter Cup again, so it will be a lot of fun.”

Ottawa has fallen just short of the Walter Cup in each of the past two seasons, losing last year’s final in four games to the Montreal Victoire after suffering the same fate against the Minnesota Frost in 2025. The challenge now is to get back to the final with a different-looking lineup.

items.t: Godfrey Phillips profit dips 44% in Q1FY27 as revenue doubles on tax shift
sum: Godfrey Phillips India saw consolidated net profit fall 44.1% to ₹198.39 crore in Q1FY27, while total income doubled to ₹3,819.56 crore due to indirect tax changes. The company received ₹10,000 lakhs in interim insurance claims and set August 11 as the dividend record date.
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.

Godfrey Phillips India Limited reported a consolidated net profit of ₹198.39 crore for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (Q1FY27), marking a 44.1% decline from ₹356.28 crore in the corresponding period last year. Despite the profitability contraction, total income from continuing operations more than doubled to ₹3,819.56 crore from ₹1,813.26 crore. This divergence was primarily driven by a revision in the indirect tax structure on cigarettes effective February 1, 2026, which significantly altered revenue composition and excise duty expenses. Shareholders will note that the Board has fixed August 11, 2026, as the record date for the payment of the final dividend for FY25-26.

The Board of Directors approved the unaudited standalone and consolidated financial results on July 27, 2026, following review by the Audit Committee and a limited review by statutory auditors S.R. Batliboi & Co. LLP under Regulation 33 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. In addition to approving the results, the Board scheduled the company’s 89th Annual General Meeting (AGM) for August 24, 2026, at 2:30 PM IST via video conferencing. The final dividend of ₹33 per equity share of ₹2 each, recommended in May 2026, awaits approval at this meeting.

Consolidated profit before tax from continuing operations stood at ₹251.10 crore, down from ₹447.99 crore in Q1FY26. Standalone profit before tax was ₹229.12 crore, compared to ₹455.17 crore in the year-ago quarter. The net profit after tax from continuing operations for the consolidated entity was ₹198.39 crore, while the standalone figure was ₹177.39 crore. Basic and diluted earnings per share (EPS) for continuing operations were ₹12.72 for the consolidated entity and ₹11.37 for the standalone entity.
The company provided an update on the fire incident at a third-party tobacco processing plant in District Prakasam, Andhra Pradesh, which occurred on October 10, 2025.

Philips Shares Air Purifier Test Findings Amid Winter Pollution
sum: Winter pollution brings renewed attention to indoor air quality and the performance of air purifiers. Versuni, which markets Philips home appliances, has released findings from an independent evaluation of seven purifier series, reporting PM2.5 reductions of up to 98.8% under high particulate concentrations.

The evaluation was conducted by NABL-accredited FARE Labs. According to Versuni, testing began at a monitor-displayed AQI reading of 2,361, with the findings supporting the company's "Tested for Indian Conditions" claim.

The evaluation covered the Philips 4200, 3200, 2200, 1000 and 900 Series, alongside the 3400 Series air purifier-humidifier and the 8000 Series 3-in-1 model. Tests were conducted in a controlled indoor environment with reference to IS 17531:2021, the Bureau of Indian Standards specification for portable indoor air purifiers. Readings were recorded at approximately 30-second intervals.

Gulbahar Taurani, MD and CEO of Versuni India, said the exercise was intended to assess the purifiers under high pollution conditions relevant to India. The company disclosed detailed particulate readings and elapsed times for three of the seven series evaluated.

The 4200 Series recorded the largest PM2.5 reduction disclosed in the announcement, with concentrations falling from 999µg/m³ to 12µg/m³ in approximately 21 minutes, a decline of 98.8%. The 3400 Series recorded a 98.5% reduction over approximately 32 minutes, while the 900 Series recorded a 97.2% reduction over approximately 25 minutes.

PM10 concentrations declined by 97.9% for the 4200 and 3400 Series, and by 96.5% for the 900 Series. The monitor-displayed AQI fell from 2,361 to 42 for the first two models and to 68 for the 900 Series. Versuni said the other four series also reduced airborne particulate levels, but did not provide their numerical results in the announcement.

FARE Labs Director C.S. Joshi said the evaluation provides data on particulate removal during testing, while results in homes may vary with room size, ventilation and pollution sources. Versuni also noted that purifier placement, filter condition and operating settings can affect performance.

Philips stock faces EUR 288 million Respironics settlement
sum: Philips is moving toward a settlement of long-running US investigations linked to its recalled Respironics sleep and respiratory devices. The company disclosed the agreement in principle with the US Department of Justice on Tuesday, November 3, while MedTech Dive reported the proposed resolution on November 4.

The agreement covers criminal and civil investigations related to the recall. Philips recorded a EUR 288 million provision for the proposed settlement, with payment expected in the first quarter of 2027. The agreement still requires final documentation, so the disclosure does not represent a completed payment or a fully executed settlement.

MedTech Dive reported that the recall involved more than 15 million devices, including continuous positive airway pressure and bilevel positive airway pressure machines as well as ventilators. The issue concerned soundproofing foam that could break down into particles and be inhaled by users.

The proposed payment would address the US Department of Justice investigations, but it does not remove every Respironics-related risk. MedTech Dive reported that the settlement is separate from a 2024 US Food and Drug Administration consent decree that restricts the sale of certain respiratory devices until Philips meets the agency's requirements.

Chief Executive Roy Jakobs said Philips was working toward a return to the US market for affected products, but that the timing ultimately depended on the FDA. The company is therefore continuing to prepare for a possible market return without controlling the authorization timetable.

The proposed settlement also excludes other proceedings, including an investigation by US state attorneys general. For investors, that distinction matters: the agreement can reduce one part of the legal overhang, but it does not establish that all recall-related liabilities have been resolved.

Philips stock traded at 27.37 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:08 CET on Friday, November 13, 0.44 percent above the Xetra close of Thursday, November 12. The comparison places the shares modestly higher during the session, without establishing that the move was caused by the settlement news.

Makeup artist draws on heritage for new palette
sum: Cover of Soualigan Divine Palette. The palette has been created in the shape of St. Maarten and weighs about 500 grams.

PHILIPSBURG--St. Peters-born makeup artist and entrepreneur Antoinette Philips is celebrating her heritage ahead of St. Maarten Day with the launch of a new eyeshadow palette inspired by the island's communities, landscapes and cultural symbols.

The palette, named Soualigan Divine, will be available from November 11 through Philips' beauty brand, VMOUR Beauty. Its 22 shades take their names from places and features associated with the island, including Grand Case, Dutch Quarter, the Salt Pond, Guavaberry and the flamboyant tree. One shade is named after St. Peters where Philips once resided.

Currently based in the Netherlands, where she works as a social worker supporting persons with disabilities, Philips developed the collection as a tribute to the island that shaped her identity. Both the palette's case design and its colours draw inspiration from St. Maarten and St. Martin as a shared island with two distinct national identities.

Soualigan Divine is the second palette released under VMOUR Beauty, which Philips established in 2024. Her first collection, VMOUR Merlot, reflected her interest in wine and makeup with packaging shaped like a wine glass.

The idea for the brand developed from informal makeup sessions with friends, often accompanied by a glass of wine. Encouraged by a mentor to share those moments online, Philips began livestreaming her makeup sessions and gradually built an audience on TikTok, where she shares makeup looks and interacts with followers.

With her latest collection, she has shifted the inspiration from wine to the Caribbean, drawing on the colours and cultural influences of her homeland. The palette combines matte and shimmer finishes, with shades intended for both everyday makeup and more dramatic looks.

Air pollution getting worse? These 6 smart air purifiers offer bedroom coverage up to 450 sq ft
sum: Delhi NCR has been facing an increasing problem of air quality due to indoor pollution in homes. On November 9, 2026, Delhi's Air Quality Index (AQI) stood at 372, placing it in the 'Very Poor' category, according to the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM), citing CPCB data. Many families are considering the use of air purifiers to improve indoor air quality, with Stage III of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) also in effect.

Consider selecting an air purifier that has sufficient room coverage, HEPA filters and smart connectivity options for individuals that spend several hours in their bedrooms. Buyers do not necessarily need to spend over ₹10,000 to get these features. There are several brands that have app-controlled models that have multi-layer filtration and are relatively budget-friendly. Let's look at the top 6 smart air purifiers available in the market and their specifications and prices in India.

The Eureka Forbes Aeroguard 400G is a 400 sq ft coverage with an activated carbon and True HEPA H13 filtration system and washable prefilter. It also has dual HEPA filtering, Wi-Fi connectivity, an aroma diffuser and 360-degree air intake.
The purifier is priced at ₹9,999 on the brand's website, and the offered discount of ₹500 is mentioned in the offer details. Consumers should verify the last check-out cost prior to purchase.

The Mijia Smart Air Purifier 4 Compact can purify an area of up to 400 sq ft based on two air changes per hour (ACPH), as per the official website of the company, Xiaomi India. It features a three-layered filter system: pre-filter, HEPA filter and activated carbon with particle CADR of 230 cubic metres per hour.

The purifier works at 20 dB in sleep mode and will be controlled remotely using the Xiaomi Home app. Google Assistant and Amazon Alexa voice controls are also available, says Xiaomi. It is available for ₹6,999 on Blinkit.

The Qubo Q450 from Hero Group offers coverage of up to 450 sq ft and a claimed CADR of 300 cubic metres per hour. It comes with a 5-in-1 filtration system which comprises a washable pre-filter, PP filter, Nano-Silver filter, activated carbon filter and True HEPA H13 filter.

What Publicis Groupe (ENXTPA:PUB)'s AI Leadership Reshuffle Means For Shareholders
sum: Publicis Groupe has reshaped its data and AI leadership around the Marcel platform, appointing senior figures such as chief client officer Rohan Philips and media planning and buying director Robin Girdhar, after prior roles at dentsu, GroupM and Times Internet.

The decision to put an AI focused client leader like Philips into a front line role indicates that Publicis wants its internal Marcel platform directly tied to client facing solutions, rather than treated as back office infrastructure.
We will look at how Publicis Groupe's investment narrative evolves as Marcel's applied AI focus becomes central to client facing work.
Scan how Publicis Groupe's AI pivot compares with other potential beneficiaries of the same trend by tracking a curated set of 53 AI infrastructure stocks in one place.

To own Publicis Groupe, you need to believe the group can keep turning its data and AI stack into dependable client demand, while holding margins near recent levels. The Marcel focused reshuffle fits that story by putting product builders into client facing roles. The near term swing factor still looks like execution on AI linked solutions and Connected Media.

The biggest near term risk remains pressure on profitability if cost inflation or pricing limits prevent progress from the 17.5% H1 2026 operating margin and 2025 levels of 18.2%. Leadership changes around Marcel do not remove that risk. They mainly refine who is accountable for delivering on it.

The Philips appointment tied directly to Marcel and applied AI for marketing looks most relevant here. Publicis Groupe is equipping the new chief client officer with a product heavy background just as the group leans on AI powered automation and targets a 25% cut to manual tasks across 114,000 employees. Hospitals are consolidating vendor relationships to streamline operations, giving Philips an advantage in pitching integrated equipment platforms. Management captured market share in North America by replacing long-standing rivals at major hospital networks.

The company is shifting hospital clients away from one-off equipment sales and toward Enterprise Monitoring as a Service (EMaaS), a model in which health systems pay recurring fees for software and hardware. That recurring model helps insulate cash flows from lumpier capital spending cycles.

sum: I’m old enough to remember the day when CVS, the big drugstore company, opted to get even bigger by acquiring the health insurer Aetna.

“Today marks the start of a new day in healthcare and a transformative moment for our company and our industry,” CVS Health President and Chief Executive Officer Larry J. Merlo boasted. The $70-billion deal would lead to “improved health outcomes and lower medical costs,” he said.
I’m not giving away my age with this recollection. The deal happened a mere eight years ago, in 2018.
Merlo’s ambitions and braggadocio didn’t have much of a shelf life: On Wednesday, the company announced it was deconstructing the edifice he had erected, by splitting into two companies.
Greater independence will make it easier to serve consumers, members, patients, and communities.

One, encompassing Aetna and Caremark, the pharmacy benefit manager it acquired in 2007 for $26.5 billion, will retain the name CVS Health, and the other, dubbed CVS Pharmacy, will own the 9,000 CVS drugstores, the nationwide legacy of the original company that started with a single Massachusetts store.

Trump Accounts: What parents need to know about automatic enrollment, $1,000 seed money and activation
sum: Whether you realize it or not, your child may be enrolled in a “Trump Account.”

Rolled out earlier this year, the Trump Accounts program allows parents to claim special investment accounts for children who are 18 years old or younger. And some babies are eligible to receive a one-time $1,000 contribution from the government.

Now, because of automatic enrollment highlighted Wednesday by President Trump, the Treasury Department says every eligible child with a valid Social Security number has a Trump Account. But parents and legal guardians would still need to formally activate the accounts if they haven’t already.

The accounts are a savings tool that invests money in the stock market on a child’s behalf. The child can’t access the money until they turn 18 and can use it only for specific purposes, such as paying tuition, starting a business or making a down payment on a home. Families can activate an account through the program’s trumpaccounts.gov website or its mobile phone app.

The government will make a $1,000 contribution for some babies after the account is claimed. To qualify for the $1,000 seed money, a baby must be a U.S. citizen, have a Social Security number and be born between Jan. 1, 2025, and Dec. 31, 2028 — covering Trump’s current term.

Any parent — regardless of their immigration status — can open an account for a qualifying child. Parents of older children also are encouraged to open accounts. Even though they aren’t eligible for the government’s $1,000 contribution, some older children are eligible for seed money of $250 drawn from separate investments from wealthy donors.

Otherwise, family contributions will need to come out of pocket. Parents can contribute up to $2,500 annually in pretax income, much like retirement accounts. Employers, relatives, friends, local governments and philanthropic groups can also pitch in. Yearly contributions are capped at $5,000, although contributions from governments and charities don’t count toward that total.

items.t: Philips looks to make India its centre of excellence for innovation
sum: Dutch major Philips is doubling down on investments in research and development activities, and aims to make India a centre of excellence for innovation across its product segments.
By the end of this decade, Philips will be completing 100 years in India, which is also a strong growth driver for its personal healthcare portfolio.

At the global level, Philips spends about 5-6 per cent of its revenue in R&D against an average 2-3 per cent in the consumer industry globally, according to Deeptha Khanna, Executive Vice President and Chief Business Leader for personal health and a member of the Royal Philips executive committee in India.

She told PTI that it was quite bullish about India's role not just in terms of the market and growth opportunity but also being a centre of excellence for the company on innovation across the entire enterprise.
"I think that (5-6 per cent) is a really substantial commitment. So, we are pretty serious about first and foremost R&D investment.

"Also, 40 per cent of our personal care portfolio in India is local for locals. So, we do expect to make sure that our investment in both R&D and marketing and distribution, among others, will support our growth ambition," she said.

Without disclosing R&D investment numbers, Khanna said, "I think the investment is the people. The majority of our digital innovation teams are sitting here already right now, and I think that promises a lot of impact in the future".

items.t: Why Exor's shares still look deeply undervalued
sum: As the owner of Ferrari, Exor controls one of the world's highest-quality luxury assets, yet its shares reflect little of that strength. The investment case rests on three components: asset quality, capital allocation, and the discount to net asset value (NAV).

Ferrari is a high-margin luxury business with gross margins of about 50%. Growth is driven by deliberate supply discipline. Production is constrained to preserve exclusivity, resulting in sustained excess demand and multi-year order backlogs. This underpins both pricing power and earnings visibility.
Returns are driven by changes in underlying asset values, capital allocation decisions, movements in the discount to NAV.
The first two have been delivered historically, although future outcomes remain uncertain.

At about 50%, the current discount is wide in both absolute and historical terms. The opportunity lies in mean reversion. A narrowing towards the historical range implies material upside, even without underlying NAV growth.
The investment case does not rely on strong macro conditions. Instead, returns are driven by portfolio execution and the potential for discount normalisation.
On balance, the odds and probabilities favour a narrowing of the discount.
